content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with a [product_name] module to read four inputs simultaneously to form a digital code, such as 0010. My challenge is that I can't lock the inputs after receiving the code, so if another input is pressed, the code changes unexpectedly. I want to block all inputs until all are reset. Does anyone have suggestions on how this can be achieved? Thanks, [user_name]
Hello, You might want to check the [product_name] Application Examples. The digital inputs password example could be helpful in your situation. Regards,

Hi, I appreciate your support. The example is interesting, but in my setup, the code is entered all at once. I have multiple switches connected, each corresponding to a different code (like 1100, 0011, 1010). For instance, if switch 0011 is pressed and then 1100 is also pressed without releasing the first, the result is 1111. My goal is to prevent changes until the initial switch is released. Thank you very much for your quick assistance. [user_name]
Consider an approach like the one shown in this example using three inputs. Note: This isn't a perfect solution. Every time input I4 is pressed, all outputs from the RS blocks briefly reset to zero.
Hello [user_name], Please refer to the attached file for possible ideas to address your question. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience difficulties managing input states on a specific hardware module, particularly around temporarily blocking input changes once a code is entered. The main concern is the lack of built-in support for locking inputs in certain logic configurations, which leads to improper code changes when multiple inputs are activated at once. Suggestions include checking documentation and application examples, but shared solutions indicate workarounds are necessary, highlighting the device's complexity and functional limitations for this application.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to lock or block inputs after a code is registered, ensuring new inputs do not alter the current code until all switches are released.
pain_keywords: lack of logic for input locking
